# simpledir

> Directory shortcuts for your shell. Named aliases for the places you actually
> go, plus frecency for the ones you never named. The next zoxide, in one C++
> file, with no interpreter and no database.

`sd` moves you and only reads your config. `sdcfg` changes things and never
changes your directory. Both names are the same binary; the program decides
which half it is by the name it was invoked as (`argv[0]`).

Linux. MIT. Zero dependencies beyond libstdc++ and `curl`.

## Docs

- [README.md](https://github.com/noxthedevwindev-greatest/simpledir/blob/main/README.md): full documentation
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/noxthedevwindev-greatest/simpledir/blob/main/AGENTS.md): notes for coding agents working on this repository
- [CONTRIBUTORS.md](https://github.com/noxthedevwindev-greatest/simpledir/blob/main/CONTRIBUTORS.md): authorship and how to contribute
- [LICENSE](https://github.com/noxthedevwindev-greatent/simpledir/blob/main/LICENSE): MIT

## Install

```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/noxthedevwindev-greatest/simpledir/main/install.sh | bash
```

The installer detects the platform, downloads a prebuilt `sd-linux-x86_64` or
`sd-linux-arm64` binary from the latest release, and **compiles from source if
there isn't one** — installing a toolchain with yay, pacman or mise first if
necessary. It appends a guarded wrapper block to `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`
(chosen from `$SHELL`). Run it again over an existing install and it reports
what it found and asks whether to repair, uninstall, or cancel.

`bash install.sh --source` forces the compile path, `--uninstall` reverses it.
`SIMPLEDIR_BIN_DIR`, `SIMPLEDIR_RC`, `SIMPLEDIR_PM`, `SIMPLEDIR_NO_RC=1`.

## Commands

`sd` — moves you, reads the config, records where you went:

```
sd <alias>                 jump (falls back to frecency if it isn't an alias)
sd -                       previous directory
sd                         $HOME
sd /some/path              a raw path, cd'd as-is
sd ls [<query>] [--long]   list jumpable aliases; --names one per line; --json the config shape
sd print <alias[/sub]>     print the directory without cd'ing
sd top [<query>] [--json]  the frecency log, best first
sd suggest [<query>]       directories from your shell history worth naming; --top N, --json
sd i [<query>]             interactive picker; fzf if installed, numbered list otherwise
```

`sdcfg` — changes things, never moves you:

```
sdcfg add [<name>] [<path>]   bind; name defaults to the directory basename, path to $PWD; --force; --keep-symlinks
sdcfg rm <name>               remove an alias
sdcfg rename <old> <new>      rename, keeping the path; --force
sdcfg import <dir>            bind every subdirectory of a tree; --depth, --prefix, --force, --hidden, --dry-run, --keep-symlinks
sdcfg bind                    create aliases from what `sd suggest` found; --top N, --dry-run
sdcfg forget                  drop directories from the visit log; --all, --missing, --path P, --yes
sdcfg migrate                migrate the config file v1 -> v2; --dry-run
sdcfg zoxide                  import the directories zoxide knows about; --bind, --top N, --dry-run
sdcfg edit [<editor>]         open the config in $EDITOR
sdcfg update                  check for a newer release, ask, then install; --check; --yes; --to vX.Y.Z
sdcfg revert                  go back to the previously installed version; --to vX.Y.Z
sdcfg releases                list the published releases
sdcfg uninstall               remove the binaries and the shell wrapper; --purge; --yes
sdcfg doctor                  report config, dead aliases, shell wiring and PATH problems; exit 1 if any
sdcfg completions bash|zsh    print a shell completion script
sdcfg init                    print the shell wrapper
```

Exit codes: `0` success, `1` unknown alias or user error, `2` argument parsing
or unknown-verb error.

All flags are long-form only; there are no short aliases. Reaching for the wrong
half is exit 2 and gets a pointer: `sd add` prints
`did you mean 'sdcfg add'? sd only reads your config.`

An alias argument may carry a path suffix: `dots/src` resolves to `<dots>/src`.
An exact alias name always wins; otherwise a **unique name prefix** is accepted
(`hy` jumps to `hypr`), and two or more candidates is an error listing them,
never a guess. An absolute path is never an alias and says so.

## Frecency

`sd <word>` falls back to the visit log when the word isn't an alias, so
`sd wev` finds a directory you never named.

Scoring: a three-day half-life, computed lazily at read time, so nothing runs in
the background. The log is written at most once per directory per minute,
pruned of anything that has faded below 0.02, and capped at 500 entries.
Matching skips directories that have a name — if you named it, `sd name` is the
way in. Recording does not skip them, so `sd top` shows real activity.

Disable with `SIMPLEDIR_NO_HISTORY=1` or `"history": false` in the config.
`sdcfg forget --all` wipes it.

## Configuration

`~/.simpledir/` holds two files:

- `config.json` — yours. plain JSON, hand-editable, or `sdcfg edit`
- `history.json` — the tool's. frecency counts. `sdcfg forget` is the honest way
  to change it

```json
{
  "version": 2,
  "history": true,
  "aliases": {
    "dots": "/home/you/dotfiles",
    "hypr": "/home/you/.config/hypr"
  }
}
```

`version: 1` configs are read as-is. `sdcfg migrate` migrates one to version 2:
it backs the file up first, keeps every alias exactly as it was, and creates an
empty history file. `--dry-run` shows what it would do. A config from a *newer*
simpledir is refused with an explanation rather than half-read.

`SIMPLEDIR_CONFIG_DIR` moves the whole directory elsewhere.

## Coming from zoxide

`sdcfg zoxide` reads zoxide's sqlite database (`$ZO_DATA_DIR/db.zdb`, or
`~/.zoxide.db`) and prints its top directories as `sdcfg add` lines; `--bind`
creates them. It needs the `sqlite3` command on `PATH`. If zoxide's database is
missing or unreadable it says where it looked.

## Shell wrapper

A subprocess cannot change the calling shell's cwd, so `sdcfg init` prints a
function that performs the `cd`, using `sd print` to resolve the path. The
function forwards `ls`, `print`, `suggest`, `i` and `top` to the binary without
changing directory, as does any `-flag`.

- no arguments: `cd $HOME`
- `-`: `cd $OLDPWD`
- an absolute path or one starting with `~`: `cd` straight to it

Functions rather than shell aliases, because bash expands aliases only in
interactive shells.

## Behavior on errors

- unknown alias: substring and similarity suggestions, exit `1`
- unknown alias with no frecency match: both are tried before giving up
- alias or alias-with-suffix resolving to a missing directory: refused, with the
  rebind command; `ls` tags it `[missing]`
- duplicate alias: refused unless `--force`, for both `add` and `rename`
- corrupt config: explains the problem, suggests removal, does not silently reset
- corrupt history log: ignored. a bad visit log must not stop a `cd`
- a failed history write: ignored, for the same reason
- `ls` with no aliases, or a filter that matches nothing: says so, exit `1`
- unknown flag or a verb belonging to the other command: exit `2`, with a pointer
- `update` when GitHub is unreachable: says so, exit `1`
- `update` never replaces a binary with a same-version or unidentifiable download
- `uninstall` without a terminal and without `--yes`: refuses rather than guessing

## Update and revert

`update` fetches the latest release, runs the downloaded file with `--version` to
confirm identity and version, and swaps it in atomically. Every install keeps
the binary it replaced at `sd.previous`; `revert` puts that back, offline.
`--to vX.Y.Z` installs a specific version.

Additionally `sd ls` and `sdcfg add` may print a one-line nudge when a newer
release is known. It is suppressed when stderr is not a terminal, when
`SIMPLEDIR_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` is set, when the cache in
`~/.simpledir/update-check.json` is younger than 24 hours, and never on the
`sd print` path.

Environment variables:

```
SIMPLEDIR_CONFIG_DIR       config directory                    (default ~/.simpledir)
SIMPLEDIR_NO_HISTORY       set to anything to stop recording visits
SIMPLEDIR_NO_UPDATE_CHECK  set to anything to disable update checks
SIMPLEDIR_BIN              override the path `update` writes to, and `uninstall` removes
SIMPLEDIR_RC               the only rc file `uninstall` and `doctor` will touch
SIMPLEDIR_HISTORY          an extra history file for `sd suggest` to read
SIMPLEDIR_NO_FZF           set to anything to make `sd i` skip fzf
SIMPLEDIR_UPDATE_URL       override the release API URL (used by the test suite)
SIMPLEDIR_UPDATE_ASSET_URL override the downloaded asset URL (used by the test suite)
```

## Uninstall

`sdcfg uninstall` removes the binary at `install_target()` and strips every
`# >>> simpledir >>>` … `# <<< simpledir <<<` span from the rc files in
`rc_candidates()`, leaving a `<rc>.bak.<timestamp>` backup. Aliases are
preserved unless `--purge` is given. Deleting the running binary is safe on unix.

`SIMPLEDIR_RC`, when set, is exclusive: it names the only rc file considered.
Otherwise candidates are guessed from `$SHELL` plus `~/.bashrc`, `~/.zshrc` and
`~/.config/fish/config.fish`.

## Version history

- 6.3.0 — config and history files are 644 instead of 744; `write_atomic` asked
  for `owner_all` on the non-executable path and that bundle includes `x`.
- 6.2.0 — the release check works at all: the API url was missing `/releases`
  so it fetched the repository object, and the hand-rolled json scan it read the
  answer with truncated every object at a `{?name,label}` inside a string.
  `update`, `update --check`, `releases` and the update nudge had never once
  succeeded.
- 6.1.0 — `update --to` and `revert` actually work: the
  release URL is built from the architecture, the release list is no longer a
  prerequisite, every historical asset name is tried, and a legacy build that
  calls itself `simpledir` is accepted.
- 6.0.0 — rewritten in C++ (one file, no interpreter; 73 ms → 0.8 ms per jump),
  frecency so it remembers directories you never named, `sd top`, `sdcfg forget`,
  config version 2 with `sdcfg migrate`, `sdcfg zoxide` to import from zoxide,
  `sdcfg revert` and `--to`, `sdcfg releases`, and an installer that detects the
  platform, downloads or compiles, and asks before touching an existing install.
- 5.0.0 — split into `sd` (moves, read-only) and `sdcfg` (writes, never moves).
- 4.0.0 — `suggest`, `i`, `--keep-symlinks`, unique-prefix matching.
- 3.1.0 — `uninstall`.
- 3.0.0 — `curl | bash` installer, `update`, `import`, `doctor`, release assets.
- 1.0.0 — `add`, `rm`, `ls`, `jump`, `init`, the shell wrapper, typo
  suggestions, atomic config writes.

## Development

```
make        # one g++ invocation over one file
make test   # 334 assertions against the compiled binary, no network
make assets # dist/ (the binary, sd.cpp, install.sh, mode 755)
make release
```

Repository layout:

```
sd.cpp              the entire program. installed as `sd`, with `sdcfg` symlinked to it
sd                  build output, gitignored
install.sh          the curl | bash installer
tests/run.sh        test suite, plain bash, drives the compiled binary
docs/demo.tape      vhs script that produces docs/demo.gif
packaging/PKGBUILD  Arch package definition
packaging/nix/      a nixpkgs expression
Makefile            binaries / install / uninstall / test / assets / release
```
